Mordy Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Mordy, Poland

Not demolished. Jewish settlement in Mordy developed from the second half of the 17th century; by 1921, 1,746 Jews made up over half the town's population, most murdered at Treblinka in 1942. The cemetery was possibly established at the end of the 18th century, though preserved tombstones confirm use by no later than 1828. Some of the last burials may have occurred in May 1945, following the murder of Holocaust survivors after liberation. Poland formally closed the cemetery in 1963; postwar, many tombstones were stolen for use as grinding discs, and unconfirmed reports suggest others were used to build a local railway ramp. In 2020, volunteers from the Cultural Heritage Foundation, with local government and resident support, carried out cleaning work at the site.
